title: Context, compaction, Agent KV and Memory
summary: The exact native journal is durable evidence. Model context is a bounded projection of that evidence plus current instructions, schemas, working context and user input. Context read policy.

headings.title: Context, compaction, Agent KV and Memory

html:
Context, compaction, Agent KV and Memory

The exact native journal is durable evidence. Model context is a bounded projection of that evidence plus current instructions, schemas, working context and user input. Context read policy constrains how stored material is accessed; it does not turn all stored data into automatic memory.

Memory tools are always available for explicit reads and writes. Tasks skip automatic memory lookup, injection, guidance, learning and inspection/completion checks by default. The composer action Special actions → Use memory inserts @use_memory, enabling that automatic workflow for the task and its continuations. Without it, the store is opened only when a Memory tool is called; asking the Agent to remember something needs no shortcut. New tasks require their own opt-in for automatic support. Code literals and escaped tokens do not activate it, and the token is reserved from Parameter Store resolution. skipped: true in memory diagnostics describes automatic support, while tool availability and explicit read/write counters remain separate.

Settings → Advanced → Context carried forward defaults to All, preserving the existing projection. Desktop Controls and mobile Agent options can choose Most recent a Rolling window of 1–24 finished runs, Use task skill, or the global default. The policy applies to Agent continuations and Conversation history (including Ask and Plan). Independent Agent tasks retain their isolation. Accepted runs and resumes retain captured settings. Summaries reuse completion output or local facts and never add an inference call. See the carry-forward guide for boundaries, diagnostics, retrieval costs and performance release gates.

Use task skill uses a separate clean-epoch projection. The always-available task_context skill exposes metadata-first browsing, scoped lexical search, bounded reads and revision-checked task notes. Each logical sub-conversation has its own notebook; Steer and Continue retain it, while independent tasks and branches are isolated. The agent must inspect first, read applicable constraints, fetch only what its next decision requires and stop retrieving when it has enough. Historical lookup covers retained authorized material beyond the capsule window. Task notes aid resumption but never amend authority or prove an execution outcome.

Full automatic history, setup, artifact and parameter blocks are omitted in this mode. Protected accepted inputs and bounded task progress remain available. Tasks explicitly using @use_memory also receive matching durable-memory keys and tags, verified learning candidates, and Saved Memory tools. A new substantive turn or Continue starts a fresh epoch; recovery, waits and pending-control replies retain it. Core instructions and ordinary current-epoch tool replies remain present.

Settings → Advanced → Task Context reads configures Unicode characters per read: 4,000 by default and 12,000 maximum initially, with Restore defaults. Both values are editable positive integers, including values above 12,000; the default cannot exceed the maximum. Accepted tasks and continuations retain their snapshot. Source restrictions and model capacity still apply. These controls do not change attached Context policy, orientation, listing/search bounds or the 4,000-character note limit. See the carry-forward guide for the tool contracts, isolation, recovery and costs.

Explicit Save to task context selections retain references to complete assistant messages within their notebook. Current source access and redaction are rechecked at preparation and dispatch; saved selections do not become instructions or execution evidence. Saved assistant task-context flows traces UI matching, idempotent save/removal, capacity failures and submission receipts.

Notebook discovery, reads and output previews traces indexing, bounded search/continuation, owner-checked source reads, output-tail recovery and disposable-index rebuilds.

Settings → Advanced → Reuse request instruction fragments reuses small immutable instruction strings within the current run. It preserves the single leading system message, current authority, tool schemas, history, exact result pages and reasoning settings. Accepted tasks retain this strict boolean across queue, resume, continuation and restart; the default is on. Off restores uncached construction with the same request layout. This setting does not manage the model server's cache. The request construction guide describes component ownership, invalidation and optional synthetic prefix diagnostics.

The canonical execution prompt in native/protocol.py teaches a bounded working set: model context is finite working memory, and tool results or script stdout may become the next model input. Inspect scope first, use the largest safe bounded batch, persist large intermediates, and retrieve exact portions when needed. Keep complete requested deliverables and necessary evidence while avoiding unnecessary raw data in the next decision. This applies across all effort levels and preserves independent parallelism. The Task Contract compiler has separate instructions.

Settings → Advanced → Context-efficient execution controls this guidance and defaults to on. The backend captures the boolean at task acceptance and retains it across resume/continue/restart. The canonical block appears once in the leading system message when enabled, and zero times when disabled; it is not repeated in stable/current task context. Projection adds the default block to pre-feature checkpoints without rewriting user messages or exact receipts. No model or tool calls implement the guidance, and it does not change observation or overflow rules.

Examples of intended execution:

Work Bounded working set
Inspect 135 Markdown files Count candidates; process bounded batches or an incremental pass; save the rename mapping; inspect ambiguous records and verify renames.
Diagnose a large log Search the relevant time/error window and read surrounding lines; expand when needed.
Generate a large report Write the complete artifact directly, verify it, and return its path, size and key findings.
Edit a large source file Find the symbol, read its region, apply a focused patch, inspect the diff and run relevant tests.
Traverse a large API Filter/select/page at the source; persist aggregates when exhaustive processing is required.
Read a large tool result Use its recovery action for the required page; automatic output uses the global head/tail allowance.

native/compaction.py budgets a coherent provider message projection without summary inference. It measures context using provider preflight when available and conservative local estimates otherwise, prunes eligible history/result groups, and retains protected current material. Manual/forced compaction and overflow recovery have explicit state. If protected inputs cannot fit, the runtime reports the capacity problem rather than claiming the omitted input was processed. Exact receipts remain in the journal. Compaction activity and timing explain changes to the projection, not deletion of work.

Stored receipts preserve every distinct captured value. For shell and Python results, an output string identical to stdout appears once in model context; both fields remain available in the stored receipt. Saved observations receive the same normalization when projected, without rewriting the journal. No distinct stdout, stderr or structured result is discarded.

Failed exchanges and their immediate corrections stay protected until recovery is proven for the same scoped operation, or trusted capability evidence explicitly supersedes the failed receipt. Only failures known not to leave uncertain external effects can become eligible. An unrelated successful script is insufficient. Open requirements, authentication/permission exchanges, unknown effects and the latest four exchanges retain their protection.

Provider counters include tool schemas and supported template options. If no exact count is available, overflow diagnostics explicitly identify a local estimate. Repeated valid provider usage can calibrate estimates downward as well as upward; the highest recent ratio and a safety margin remain in force.

Execution budgeting uses the run's pinned execution_output_reservation_tokens. An explicit max_completion_tokens request override sets that reservation; Provider Default omits the wire limit but retains the existing internal output allowance as a reservation. Preflight, compaction, context reads and goal echo use the same execution reservation. Internal inference retains client.max_tokens and its phase-specific Task Contract/recovery profile. The execution map, profile, version and reservation are deep-copied into effective_model and resume_context; global Settings changes cannot silently retune a resumed run.

Agent KV is an always-available task-local scratchpad for temporary working data with explicit kv.put, kv.get, kv.search, kv.list and kv.delete operations. It survives restart and compaction, and remains available to that task’s follow-ups. A new task in the same conversation gets a fresh KV context. Data is not automatically retrieved or injected. Guidance recommends non-secret scratch work, but storage accepts literal text without secret classification. The active Controller RAM owner, or standalone SQLite for an unowned path, applies revision compare-and-set, quotas, lazy expiry and deletion fences. Per-task put revision counters prevent stale identities from becoming valid after key deletion or expiry followed by recreation. See the KV guide for the authoritative limits, schemas, scope binding, storage ownership and cleanup flow. Its sequences trace task binding, atomic puts, explicit reads and scope retirement.

During multi-step work, the Agent is instructed to save changed, useful working data after meaningful discoveries or completed stages, before context fills up. Checkpoints contain concise decisions, partial results, remaining work, cursors and source references. The Agent must check save success, update stable keys, batch related data and skip unchanged or trivial writes.

When using Task Context, the handoff or books retain a compact index of relevant KV keys and their purpose. After compaction, reset or resume, the Agent reads only entries needed for the next step; it can use kv.list or kv.search if the index is missing. Large payloads stay in files/results/artifacts, with references and compact conclusions in KV. Each value is limited to 16 KiB, with at most 256 entries and 512 KiB per task. Tool output must still be bounded before execution; storing it later cannot repair an already oversized model input. These are model guidance requirements, with no automatic KV writes, auxiliary inference or new execution gate.

Working Context records verified setup/resource facts with capability-owned access and publication. These facts are neither fresh external observations nor unrestricted credential storage. Use the owning capability to validate current external state.

The command setup guide explains the Git, SSH, Kubernetes and SLURM adapters, their Gateway observations and stale-identity rules.

Verified setup and source associations

Working Context retains at most eight setup records. Normalization checks schema version, exact fields, registered capability kind, provenance IDs, finite verification time and the setup-derived resource key. Each record, including associated-source metadata, must fit 4,096 bytes of canonical JSON. Invalid or oversized entries are omitted; they are not repaired into verified setup. The retained order is insertion/refresh order, not a sort by timestamps.

Capability adapters validate setup, decide which older records are superseded, project public fields and recheck Gateway compatibility. Matching connection failures can mark a record stale; an application-level error response does not necessarily invalidate a connection. Publication mutates the owned run state and emits events; the surrounding run owner supplies persistence. It does not open a connection, extract memory from prose or perform a helper-model call.

Ordinary inheritance requires both turns to use Conversation mode, the same artifact scope and a non-abandoned source. Independent Agent requests do not inherit setup through that path. Agent runs can still record verified setup for explicit continuations. Model projection supports Conversation mode and continuations with limited carry-forward, omits abandoned state, and considers newest records first. The 12,000-character bound covers the serialized projected resource list; associated guidance is added separately. Omission counts remain visible.

Optional resource-associated Context is resolved from explicit source IDs. It remains reference material under its own grants and availability checks, rather than fresh execution evidence. Removing a setup record does not delete the uploaded body. See Context storage and read policy for those ownership boundaries and Working Context fixtures for bounds, stale-state transitions and adapter isolation.

Conversation branches and historical context

Conversation handoff validates a version-two seed whose bounded capsules end at the exact selected source request. It carries historical intent/outcome, branch lineage, attachment metadata, an optional notebook branch descriptor and references to retained results. It does not make source credentials, live handles, pending operations or job ownership into authority for the new conversation.

First-checkpoint hydration checks the target conversation's seed claim. Compatible artifact scope permits verified setup in Conversation mode; each historical receipt link additionally needs an independently committed grant and an existing source artifact. The seed itself cannot grant access. Preparation can defer link and claim writes to the first-checkpoint transaction. A later independent Agent request retains normal isolation; when Conversation mode returns, bounded branch-owned history can be recovered from the branch's first run unless manual compaction or existing lineage prevents restoration.

handoff_history is the target branch's separately retained public archive. Its reader respects conversation tombstones and supports JSON Pointer selection. Offset and limit count serialized JSON characters, with a default of 6,000 and a maximum of 12,000. The RAM/pointer paths serialize decoded data; plain SQL reads page the stored JSON. Offsets therefore belong to that selected representation, not a universal byte cursor for the original conversation journal.

Structural handoff projection removes internal reasoning/control fields, live-handle fields and reasoning markup, with depth and per-string limits. Its compatibility secrets arguments do not substitute credential values. Ordinary historical text can remain literal; optional credential redaction is governed by the separate redaction policy. Selected content-sensitive capability receipts use structural-only projection. When receipt data is filtered, it is marked incomplete rather than presented as the original full result.

Historical unknown effects remain separate from active unknown operations. A matching replay fingerprint stays unresolved until a fresh, complete, executed, non-stale external read covers all recorded written resources. Unrelated reads and elapsed time are insufficient. Branch fixtures cover selected-history boundaries, source deletion, independent grants, rollback, Agent/Conversation isolation and this reconciliation rule. Same-task FIFO continuations use a separate single-child ownership path.

Durable cross-conversation Memory

Memory is a built-in skill whose tools are always available. Desktop and mobile capability controls label it Built in · Always enabled. Explicit requests to read, store or manage memory work without @use_memory; the token enables automatic recall, injection, guidance, checks and proactive learning. Execution restrictions still apply, and Advisory mode permits local Memory.

For an opted-in task, the main Agent proactively saves verified reusable learning during work. The user does not have to say “remember.” Corrected CLI syntax after verified success, known-good commands, workarounds, compatibility quirks and stable environment/project conventions are strong candidates. This is selective learning, not a journal: transient PIDs, load, temporary paths, unresolved failures, guesses, transcripts and raw outputs should not be copied. A user instruction not to remember information takes precedence. Optional learning must not delay critical recovery or claim persistence when storage fails.

The routine is recall → learn → save. Stable user preferences and verified project conventions can qualify without a prior failure. When a topic first emerges during work, search with a few exact metadata terms or aliases, then explicitly get useful values. Search uses AND semantics, so every term must match; long prose questions usually do not. Tags should include relevant aliases and singular/plural variants that later requests use. No qualifying lesson means no write. Most runs need zero to two durable lessons.

After a definite failed operation followed by a materially different successful attempt in the same literal executable/resource family, the runtime supplies a small learning opportunity in the next ordinary decision. The Agent writes the meaning; the runtime never extracts or saves a lesson itself. Help/version calls, identical retries, opaque commands, unrelated resources and incomplete or unknown outcomes do not prove corrections. At most four pending and eight resolved candidates are retained, using a 16-operation correlation window and a 1,200-character projection. Only operation IDs, hashes and safe metadata are retained, never commands, output or values. Fingerprints use only safe execution semantics; credentials, protected inputs, approvals and connection references cannot distinguish retries. Shell identity uses parsed executable/argv and target scope; structured tools require resource identity and approved schema enums. Uncertain identity produces no candidate. Foreground and definite durable-job terminal receipts use the same observer; a durable job marker prevents repeated learning on reconciliation. Recent explicit retrievals can identify a canonical key/revision for refinement. An ambiguous put does not resolve all candidates. Two consumable metadata search hints per run can identify newly encountered literal executables; a successful bounded cat result containing only a literal tool=identifier or executable: identifier declaration can also suggest that exact term. Arbitrary output is not indexed or retained. Accepted recall bundles stay pinned between recall triggers.

Candidate state survives ordinary continuation and runtime reconstruction. A fresh Restart, like a new conversation/fork, deliberately does not inherit pending candidates from abandoned execution. Optional candidates do not impose a completion requirement.

skills/memory/skill.py owns this guidance. It appears once through generic selected-skill context before tool choice when the skill is selected. The normal main Agent chooses memory.put; there is no extractor, classifier, post-run summarizer or background consolidator. Ordinary Agent tool decisions may consume ordinary inference turns; Memory introduces zero auxiliary model calls.

Tool Contract
memory.put Require key, value, nonempty top-level tags, and top-level recall containing a nonblank summary, kind, scope, and basis. Optional expected_revision and top-level review_id/source_refs; return metadata only.
memory.get Explicitly retrieve an exact value and its revision as historical prior_note evidence.
memory.assess Record relevance after complete content delivery; optional action notes are advisory.
memory.resolve Deprecated compatibility acknowledgement; validation is not required and no state changes.
memory.search AND-match distinct exact ASCII identifiers against key/tag metadata; at most 50 results, no value snippets.
memory.list Installation-wide inventory: lexical metadata pages (at most 100), authoritative saved_records count, global_revision, scope and normalized filters; cursor is bound to the literal prefix and exact tag filters.
memory.delete Delete a record, terms and recall descriptor, optionally checking its revision.
task_context.review_epoch Freeze and page through retained authorized epoch evidence; return a durable review ID and coverage gaps.
memory.publish_epoch Validate reviewed lesson revisions and commit a stand-alone handoff and coverage manifest.

Put/get/search/list/publish_epoch and review_epoch are core-advertised when allowed. Delete uses ordinary skill discovery. memory.list returns scope="installation". Its saved_records counts all records in the active store, regardless of recall candidates, filters or page size. A filtered page can therefore be empty while saved_records is nonzero. The page, count and global_revision share one snapshot; subsequent pages observe the then-current store revision. Omit filters and follow next_cursor to enumerate every key. Writes/deletes are internal effects; reads do not prove that an external resource is currently online or configured. Fresh observations override stale Memory. Refine an existing canonical lesson with get, merge and revision-checked put; avoid .new/.fixed duplicates and unchanged rewrites. A successful Memory receipt is not itself new learning. Identical canonical JSON, effective tags and recall descriptor return unchanged=true, without changing the revision, timestamps, provenance or term index. Revision checks run first, so a stale expected_revision still conflicts even for identical content. Every model-issued write, including an update, supplies its tags and recall metadata. Missing, empty, invalid or misplaced required fields return a tool-argument rejection before persistence. The model receives the field and constraint to correct and retries the call through the ordinary tool loop. Fields inside value do not satisfy top-level metadata requirements. Direct adapter calls enforce the same contract even with generic strict-schema checks disabled. Legacy storage/import operations retain their existing tag and recall preservation rules.

Memory opts into the generic selected-skill guidance projection before tool choice. The catalog includes a whole block only when an owned permitted tool is exposed and the skill is available, then removes that block from tool descriptions. Other skills keep their existing placement unless they opt in. Blocks are limited to 4,000 characters each and 8,000 total; blocks that cannot fit retain their tool placement. This uses one authoritative copy, is included in context accounting, and makes no inference call.

For tasks using automatic Memory, a leading explicit persistence imperative activates the specialized receipt check at completion. Default-skipped tasks bypass that check; their explicit save requests remain ordinary task requirements. In either case, the Agent must not claim a successful save without successful persistence. The check does not enable an excluded capability. Quoted examples and optional learning do not create this specialized requirement.

Memory storage and recall indexes

The Server bootstraps Memory into its Controller RAM hub. MemoryStore(path) resolves the existing owner for that path; supplying a hub explicitly selects the same RAM repository. Live reads use coherent RAM views, and mutations publish entries, revisions and derived indexes atomically. A RAM-owned store rejects live SQL access. The dedicated <controller state directory>/agent_memory.db is the recovery path; standalone callers without a registered hub use its SQLite implementation. Recovery schema version 4 accepts upgrades from v2/v3 and indexes existing authored summaries without changing their entry revisions or private values. See State and recovery for the broader checkpoint lifecycle.

Both implementations use global normalized-key identity and a monotonic store-wide revision allocator. Keys use the same 1–160 ASCII character grammar as KV (letters/digits/._:-), normalized to lowercase. Up to 32 tags of 1–64 characters use the same grammar, deduplicated and sorted. Values may be objects, arrays, strings, finite numbers, booleans or null, with a 1 MiB canonical UTF-8 JSON limit. Transactions replace entries, indexed terms and the indexed recall side table atomically. Descriptor edits advance revision; changing the value without updating recall disables its previous summary. Deletes advance the store revision and remove recall data when the record exists. Deleting an absent record is an unchanged result unless an expected revision requires it to exist. Recreating a key receives a later revision, so an old compare-and-set cannot become valid again. No-op detection compares canonical value, effective tags, descriptor and scope; provenance differences alone do not update a record. Observer delivery happens after commit, and an observer failure cannot undo a successful write.

The storage layer permits omitted tags and recall for compatibility/import callers. It preserves omitted tags on updates; omitted recall survives only unchanged values, while explicit null clears it. Model-issued tools retain the stricter metadata requirements above. The internal epoch-publication path can return an existing destination unchanged; new publication checks its referenced lesson revisions inside the same transaction.

Search and list return metadata without reading JSON values. get returns the exact value explicitly; the human editor has a separate coherent snapshot of editable values and provenance. List cursors bind normalized prefix, exact tag and last key, not a historical snapshot: later pages see the then-current store. The count and revision returned with each page describe that page's snapshot.

Metadata matching is lexical, with no embeddings or model calls. Input tokenization uses at most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes and 128 distinct lowercase ASCII identifiers. Explicit search matches every whole identifier against keys/tags and returns at most 50 records. Recall also considers segments and authored summary terms, filters project scope, and admits full-key, tag or summary hits, or two distinct matching key terms. Fixed scores favor a full key, then tags, key segments and summary terms; ties use matched-term count, latest update and lexical key order. Private value text is never an index input.

Scoped recall returns every matching candidate with the store revision. Eligible authored summaries require observed/user-provided basis; hypotheses, questions and non-user-provided preferences require explicit retrieval instead. Project summaries need a bound scope derived from stable Gateway/local identity and an absolute root. This hash selects recall candidates; it grants no access. Missing/ineligible summaries remain key/revision references with a retrieval reason. The older match_metadata / matching.project path instead caps matches at 24 and its complete serialized field at 2,000 characters; those legacy limits do not bound current scoped recall.

Owner Responsibility
Memory store facade and SQLite backend Owner selection, standalone transactions and recovery schema
RAM Memory store Atomic entry/index publication, coherent reads and derived-index rebuild
Storage validators Identity grammar, strict JSON, byte limits and safe failures
Lexical matching Tokens, weights and legacy bounded projection
Recall descriptor contract Descriptor eligibility, scope and value-change retention

Source conversation/run IDs are provenance only. Restart, compaction, branching and ordinary conversation deletion leave Memory intact. Forks access the same store; handoff does not copy Memory records or create a branch snapshot of its values.

Agent Checks includes Memory inspection before work (completion.memory_assessment), which defaults OFF, including for existing tasks without an explicit setting. Its stored ID and scope support (global, conversation, prompt and run) are unchanged. When OFF, the Agent chooses the order of memory and task work; initial inspection remains guidance. For a task using automatic Memory, ON requires every runtime-selected candidate to be retrieved, delivered to an accepted model decision, and explicitly assessed before task work. Keys/tags and retrieval receipts alone do not establish inspection. Truncated contents require complete coverage through read_result or task_context.read. The runtime verifies delivery and assessment, not comprehension. Both historical retrieval modes (relevant, all) use this routine.

The main Agent calls controller-local memory.assess with key, revision, decision and explanation. All relevance decisions remain available: not_applicable, context_only, overridden and applicable_action. Action declarations are optional for every decision. Legacy action timing and evidence fields are accepted as advisory metadata; capability contracts, argument checks and expected receipts are not required or validated. Assessments never create enforceable obligations. Current instructions, fresh evidence and permissions take precedence over memory.

Memory application is best effort. Initial inspection and remembered action notes do not block ordinary, direct, implicit or Plan-mode completion. The Agent finishes the actual task without a final memory audit, receipt matching or resolution loop. Successful actions must never be repeated merely to repair memory bookkeeping. Explicit user-requested actions remain task requirements, and explicit “remember/save this” requests still require successful persistence before success can be claimed.

memory.resolve remains callable for older instructions. A valid legacy call returns {"validation_required": false, "status": "not_required"} without reading receipts, fulfilling actions, changing task status, emitting resolution events or incrementing rejection counters. It is deprecated and unnecessary.

When inspection is ON, mixed memory-read/task-work decisions are rejected before dispatch. Recovery reads, discovery, permissions, user interaction, completion, Stop and cancellation remain available. Three consecutive initial inspection rejections without ledger progress stop attempted task work as partial. Reads, delivery and assessments can clear the strike counter, as can accepted scope, intent or availability transitions. Neither before_work nor before_completion action notes participate in this guard.

The task-owned ledger retains retrieval, delivered coverage and relevance assessments across resume. Changed revisions require fresh inspection; changed instructions require reassessment. Existing obligation records and execution receipts remain historical data for diagnostics. Model context shows initial inspection progress and relevance decisions, without pending action obligations or proof checklists. Restoring an unfinished run clears obsolete memory-completion rejection feedback; completed and partial historical tasks are not reopened. Old proof feedback is also retired in projected model history; the original journal and execution receipts remain unchanged. No destructive migration is required. Queue scheduling is unchanged: dependent work starts on the backend after its predecessor completes.

The shared recall service matches exact key/tag terms and authored recall-summary terms at task/epoch boundaries. Summary matching excludes common connective/request words and never indexes raw JSON values. Recall descriptors retain summary (at most 600 characters), kind, scope, basis, and optional source_refs; summaries remain useful for deterministic matching but are not injected into prompts. Matching uses bounded accepted user input and task-book topics, without scanning full history or arbitrary output. Every match is retained in rank order without a record-count cap. Project-bound records from other projects remain excluded; profile scope supports portable lessons. Explicit memory.search remains an exact key/tag search across scopes.

Automatic preparation reads metadata only, performs zero memory.get calls and zero model calls, and supplies one compact durable_memory block with retrieval mode, guidance, and {key, revision, tags} entries. Matching owned retrieval references and bounded recovery hints can accompany those entries. No summaries, values or provenance bodies are injected. Capability selection and contract compilation receive the same candidates, with retrieval deferred to the executing Agent. The Agent batches independent gets, applies relevant retrieved knowledge, and gives current user instructions and fresh observations precedence. Missing/unavailable memories do not invite repeated attempts.

The complete candidate list survives optional progress compaction and must still fit the provider request. Increasing memory value size does not increase initial prompt size. Explicit task_context.resume retains paged metadata references. New topics and relevant failures can trigger at most two extra refreshes while the current selection is healthy and its store revision is unchanged. Epoch/project boundaries reset this topic budget; store-revision changes and recovery from unavailable selection can refresh beyond it. Scope and store-revision checks invalidate stale references; a concurrent selection change is retried once. Older content caches rebuild as metadata before projection. Successful explicit gets retain task- and revision-bound result references across later turns and compaction. The Agent reuses these results, reading missing details through task_context.read rather than fetching again. Metadata delivery increments references_delivered; only successful explicit gets increment memory_reads. Metadata is neither delivered content nor proof of reuse.

A direct request such as “save everything learned this epoch” binds a durable source epoch. A save-only follow-up selects its preceding epoch; a combined work-and-save request selects the working epoch. An explicit tce_… reference can select an older authorized epoch. Quoted examples, hypothetical questions and tool output do not bind this requirement.

The main Agent calls task_context.review_epoch and follows every cursor. The review freezes retained user messages, visible assistant messages, tool evidence and authored fact/work changes; it neither reruns tools nor fetches external resources. Pages honor notebook ownership, source restrictions, redaction and read limits. Only page ranges actually delivered to a successful model decision count as reviewed. The accepted epoch request is also a valid source reference when the runtime verifies that it contains exactly the same reviewed user text; arbitrary aliases are rejected. Review progress survives compaction, checkpoint recovery and backup. Changed or unavailable sources, retention gaps and unresolved operations are explicit in the result.

Comprehensive consolidation has no zero-to-two-lesson limit. Save distinct reusable lessons, decisions with rationale, observed failed approaches, preferences and labeled uncertainties. Put review_id and supporting source_refs outside value, alongside key, and preserve canonical records with revision-checked updates. Then call memory.publish_epoch with every saved key/revision and a handoff containing objective, completed work, remaining work, uncertainties and next step. Publication validates revisions inside the Memory transaction; deterministic manifest identity makes retries safe even if the separate notebook publication checkpoint fails.

A complete manifest is required for a successful comprehensive-save outcome. Unrelated puts do not satisfy it. Partial publication remains possible, but the final outcome must report incomplete coverage and remaining work. A fully reviewed epoch with no new reusable lessons may publish zero lessons plus its handoff. Complete coverage proves that all available authorized evidence was delivered for review; it cannot prove the model extracted every possible insight. Manifests and handoffs are ordinary global Memory records, usable by another conversation without access to the source notebook.

The existing /status panel and run snapshot expose Memory policy and current-run receipt counters; opted-in status also reads the current saved-record count and global revision. Automatic matches, delivered-reference counters, lookup latency, reviewed source counts and publication status are tracked separately. Metadata matches, explicit gets, writes and unchanged writes are separate facts. Last write/retrieval entries are scoped to the current run and backed by actual successful receipts. No value is displayed; matching alone is never reported as retrieval or successful reuse. Default-skipped tasks return explicit-tool diagnostics without opening automatic inventory status. Active status delegates to the current RAM owner or an existing standalone store without creating an absent store. Recall preparation checks the revision token and queries matching metadata only when selection needs a refresh.

Sensitive JSON is allowed. Keep secrets out of keys/tags because those are automatically visible metadata. Put receipts, search/list and diagnostic events never include values. Automatic context contains keys, revisions and tags only. The Agent must explicitly retrieve values to inspect them; retrieved values are model-visible historical context, not Parameter Store private binding. Existing runtime redaction/provenance policy applies; Memory adds no implicit redaction. Local sensitive-store creation uses restrictive file permissions where supported; Memory adds no encryption/keychain layer. Large explicit get results retain the ordinary bounded observation/exact receipt retrieval behavior.

Example:

  1. In Conversation A, the user enables Use memory (@use_memory) and asks the Agent to use fdfind, without separately asking it to remember. An invocation fails; the Agent inspects usage, verifies the corrected command, and saves tools.fdfind.usage with a scoped recall summary and tags such as fdfind, fd, fd-find, files and cli.
  2. In Conversation B, the user again enables Use memory for a new fdfind task. Matching surfaces candidate metadata. The Agent calls memory.get to retrieve the value, reuses any owned result reference for missing pages, and checks current behavior when relevant. The authored summary helps select candidates but is not injected.

Memory runtime ownership and acceptance

The store, retrieval references and inspection ledger answer different questions: what is saved, which explicit read produced evidence, and which authorized contents reached an accepted model decision. A successful get advances retrieval; it does not alone prove delivery. memory.assess stages the complete batch before committing, so an invalid item cannot leave earlier items assessed. Identical repeated assessments do not count as new progress.

flowchart TD A[Accepted task policy and user input] --> B[Prepare metadata candidates] B --> C[Explicit memory.get] C --> D[Authoritative receipt and owned reference] D --> E[Project full value or exact authorized pages] E --> F[Accepted decision commits delivery coverage] F --> G[Atomic memory.assess relevance batch] G --> H[Optional inspection check admits task work] D --> I[Safe receipt metadata and learning candidates] I --> J[Main Agent chooses whether to save a lesson] J --> K[Explicit revision-checked memory.put]

Coverage is bound to the task scope, intent, value revision and exact representation. Ranges from different representations cannot be combined, and reading only the final page is insufficient. A complete authorized redacted view can establish delivery; neither the ledger nor its diagnostics stores the body. The coverage capture happens outside the ledger lock, and acceptance checks identity again before committing it. Events are published after releasing the lock.

Changed intent retires assessments; a changed value revision requires retrieval and delivery again. Previously selected candidates remain in the inspection ledger across temporary selection unavailability. Recovery hints reuse owned receipts and request the first missing page, while normal result readers still enforce access rights. Learning observes only committed receipts and can request metadata refreshes. It has no model call or automatic write path; the executing Agent owns lesson meaning.

Implementation owner Responsibility

Tool result preview

Settings → Tool result preview and mobile Advanced expose Head characters and Tail characters, both 6,000 by default. A tool response receives one allowance, including a sequence's combined output. Strings remain text; other non-image payloads are serialized to text. Excerpts can split JSON records. Short results appear once; long results have an explicit omitted-middle marker. Content limits count Unicode characters independently of metadata and transport escaping.

Only essential outcome, coverage and recovery metadata accompanies automatic output. Runtime checks, persistence, diagnostics and Activity continue using structured receipts. For job-backed output the preview reads the actual retained log through the authorized log reader, with its original Gateway and recorded extent. The bounded receipt is unchanged. A fallback receipt excerpt is labelled as such; its beginning is not the beginning of the full log.

Concrete {tool, arguments} recovery actions name read_result, manage_job or the existing source reader. Receipt reads cannot recover bytes absent from that receipt; job logs use byte cursors, while receipt pages use their existing character offsets. Explicit requested pages keep their content, limits and continuation without another head/tail cut. An oversized page returns the existing smaller-page recovery response. Completed commands are never rerun to retrieve output.

Settings apply at the next model-input preparation, including existing tasks. Previews are rebuilt from permitted retained sources. Normal context selection and compaction run first. If necessary, automatic previews shrink proportionally while retaining the head/tail ratio and zero-valued sides. The model sees the shortening and delivered counts. If required context and usable previews still cannot fit, preflight reports an explicit capacity failure. Detailed counts and metadata sizes live in diagnostics.

Task Skill keeps its context selection, epochs, preceding replies, progress summaries and read policies. Its requested pages are explicit reads and are not clipped by the preview policy. Automatic operation progress supplies one preferred output-recovery route: a backing-log read when the receipt is incomplete, otherwise the receipt's field continuations. Routine pointer and invocation inventories remain available in explicit notebook reads instead of repeating in every model request. Receipt pages report their backing-log byte coverage separately from their own JSON character cursors. Image transport is unchanged.
